topic: Fitting rehab into a busy week

slides.headline: Back at work and rehab's slipped?
slides.sub: How to keep your exercises going in a full week.

slides.title: Shorter sessions still count
slides.body: Ten focused minutes most days often beats one long session you keep skipping. Ask your practitioner which two or three exercises matter most right now.

slides.title: Stack exercises onto habits
slides.body: Do calf raises while the kettle boils, a few squats before your shower, or a stretch after brushing your teeth. Linking exercises to daily routines makes them easier to remember.

slides.title: Plan your week on Sunday
slides.body: Pop rehab into your calendar like a meeting. Choose specific days and times, and have a short version ready for the days that get away from you.

slides.title: Make it easy to start
slides.body: Keep a band near your desk or a mat by the bed. Removing small barriers makes it much more likely that you'll actually do the exercises.

slides.title: Tell us what's realistic
slides.body: If your program doesn't fit your life, tell our team. We'd rather adjust it to something you can stick with than give you a plan you can't keep up.

slides.headline: Need a plan that fits?
slides.body: Our team at Hybrid Physiotherapy builds rehab around your schedule, with programs you can do at home, at work or at the gym. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Back at work after the summer break and your rehab exercises have quietly disappeared?

Most people find it hard to keep exercises going once the week fills up. The good news is that short, regular sessions usually work better than long ones you keep putting off.

Try stacking exercises onto things you already do, booking rehab into your calendar like a meeting, keeping a band at your desk, and having a short version ready for busy days. If your program doesn't fit your life, let us know so we can adjust it.

Our team at Hybrid Physiotherapy is happy to help. Book online via the link in bio.
